Let me analyze this conflict.

The register says applicant is "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." and the document says "MINEBEA CO., LTD."

Are these the same entity? Minebea Co., Ltd. is a Japanese company (precision manufacturer). MinebeaMitsumi Inc. is the company formed after Minebea acquired Mitsumi Electric in 2017 and renamed itself. The certificate is from 2017.

Interesting: the certificate document (PDF from 2017) says "MINEBEA CO., LTD." — Minebea changed its name to MinebeaMitsumi Inc. effective April 1, 2017. The OIML-CS register says "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." — likely the register reflects the current (renamed) name, while the certificate document reflects the name at issuance time.

So is this "same-entity"? It's the same corporate entity, just renamed. The rules say: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." A corporate rename (Minebea Co., Ltd. → MinebeaMitsumi Inc.) is arguably more than spelling drift — but it's clearly the same company, not a "genuinely different company." The rule for different-entity says "Genuinely different company or person names" — Minebea Co., Ltd. and MinebeaMitsumi Inc. are not genuinely different companies; it's a name change of the same legal entity (Minebea Co., Ltd. renamed to MinebeaMitsumi Inc. in 2017).

Hmm, but is it unverifiable from the document alone? The instruction set gives four verdicts: same-entity, different-entity, document-noise, unverifiable. External knowledge: Minebea Co., Ltd. is the former name of MinebeaMitsumi Inc. (renamed April 2017). The certificate is issued in 2017 (issuing_year: 2017), address Fujisawa-shi, Kanagawa — that's Minebea's headquarters location. So the address corroborates it's the same entity.

Given the fusion rules:
- same-entity: best value? The rules specify for number/year format differences, same-entity uses register's canonical form. For same-entity generally, likely register canonical form is best (register is curated). Actually the rules only explicitly say best_value for document-noise = register, different-entity = document. For same-entity, presumably register canonical form (the register is the database row; canonical form from register).
- different-entity: document value.

The decision: same-entity (corporate rename; Minebea Co., Ltd. became MinebeaMitsumi Inc. in April 2017; the register tracks the current legal name). Best value: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." from the register — since it's the current canonical name and the register is the authoritative source. Actually wait — should best_value be the document's since the certificate is the legal instrument? The rule says document wins only for "genuinely different" entities. For same-entity, register canonical form seems intended.

But could one argue "different-entity"? The names are genuinely different strings, but the rule's intent is "genuinely different company" — i.e., two different companies. Minebea and MinebeaMitsumi are the same company pre/post rename. Given the certificate year is 2017, the rename happened April 2017 — certificate 17.02 might be issued early 2017 (February? "17.02" suggests 2017 second certificate) under old name Minebea Co., Ltd. So the document reflects the historical legal name at issuance. Register reflects current name. Same legal entity.

Verdict: same-entity. Best value: register's "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." — because the register holds the canonical, up-to-date name of the same corporate entity.

Alternatively one could pick unverifiable — can't verify rename from the document alone? But the address "1-1-1, Katase, Fujisawa-shi, Kanagawa" matches MinebeaMitsumi's HQ. Also applicant field in the register and document's manufacturer. I'll go with same-entity and explain the rename.

One sentence why: "Minebea Co., Ltd. is the pre-2017 name of MinebeaMitsumi Inc. (corporate rename, same legal entity, corroborated by the Fujisawa HQ address), so keep the register's current canonical name."
